codexQuotaProtection.title: Official quota protection
codexQuotaProtection.help: Pause new official requests when either usage threshold is reached; third-party models remain available. Covers OpenAI official requests through CA Switch local routing only. Usage is read from the quota information official responses already carry, so normal use adds no extra requests; only the first request, or one after about 5 idle minutes, triggers a separate quota lookup. When usage can't be determined (network problems, expired login, and so on) requests go through as usual instead of being blocked. Requests already admitted and other apps can still push usage past a threshold; while paused, ordinary-quota exhaustion won't activate Luna Reserve.
codexQuotaProtection.hint: Pause at either cutoff. Defaults: 95% / 98%. Saved changes apply to new requests immediately.

settings.preserveCodexOfficialAuthOnSwitch: Keep official login for direct switches
settings.preserveCodexOfficialAuthOnSwitchDescrip: Controls third-party switches when local routing is off. Takeover routing always preserves the OpenAI official login.
settings.unifyCodexSessionHistoryDescription: Affects the OpenAI CLI only: its resume list shows only the current provider's sessions. When enabled, the official subscription runs under the shared "custom" provider id so official and third-party sessions appear in one list. The OpenAI desktop app can show all sessions since a recent update, so desktop-only users don't need this. You can optionally migrate existing official sessions in (backed up first) and restore them from backup when turning it off. Note: resuming an old session across providers may fail because its encrypted_content reasoning can only be decrypted by the backend that created it.
settings.codexStackClassicSubagentsDescription: Must be on when the main agent and a sub-agent use different providers, or the sub-agent cannot receive its task.
settings.codexStackClassicSubagentsForcedV2: OpenAI config.toml turns on [features] multi_agent_v2, which takes precedence over this setting, so it has no effect.
settings.codexSessionCompressionDescription: When on, OpenAI compresses session files that haven't changed for 7 days in the background each time it starts, which saves a lot of disk space. OpenAI decompresses a session automatically when you continue it. CA Switch still lists and counts compressed sessions; the list just doesn't show a preview of their last reply. This is a OpenAI feature still under development: OpenAI shows a notice on every start while it's on. Requires a recent OpenAI version and takes effect after restarting OpenAI. Turning it off stops compressing; sessions already compressed stay as they are.

usage.speedHelp: Output tokens per second, from the first token to the end. Only requests through the routing service with at least 100 output tokens count; for models that hide their reasoning it's an approximation. A value with ≈ is estimated from session-log timestamps when routing is off: the wait for the first token is included, so the number reads low. Only requests with at least 200 output tokens are estimated.
usage.speedSumHelp: Total output tokens divided by total generation time, not an average of per-request speeds, so short requests don't skew it. Only requests through the routing service with at least 100 output tokens count. A value with ≈ is estimated from session logs (it includes the wait for the first token, and only requests with at least 200 output tokens count) and is shown only when the row has no routed data.
usage.firstTokenHelp: Time from the routing service receiving the request to the upstream starting its output. A value with ≈ is derived from session-log timestamps when routing is off: it starts from when the previous log line was written, so it includes the client's own request preparation and reads high. Anthropic only yields one when the reply starts with thinking; OpenAI only with newer logs, and not when the reply opens with a tool call.
usage.firstTokenSumHelp: Time from the routing service receiving a request to the upstream starting its output. The row shows the median across its requests, so an occasional slow request (queueing, cold start) doesn't pull it up. Only successful streaming requests through the routing service count; requests older than 30 days, already folded into daily rollups, don't. A value with ≈ is derived from session logs (it reads high, and only some requests yield one) and is shown only when the row has no routed data.

help.route: Routing: requests go through CA Switch on this machine, unlocking hot-switching providers, failover, format conversion, and other advanced features.
